candidate.blueprint_topic: Management of Care — multidisciplinary cancer treatment planning and team collaboration
candidate.educational_objective: Explain the purpose of a multidisciplinary tumor board as coordinated clinical review by multiple cancer-care disciplines that informs, rather than replaces, patient-centered treatment planning.

options.A: Specialists from different disciplines review the case together and develop a coordinated treatment recommendation that can be discussed with the client by the treating team.
options.B: The tumor board replaces the client's treating clinicians and makes a final treatment decision that does not require further discussion with the client.
options.C: The meeting is primarily administrative and is used to schedule procedures rather than to review clinical information and treatment options.
options.D: Only one oncology specialty reviews the case so that differing perspectives do not complicate the treatment plan.

candidate.rationale: The National Cancer Institute defines tumor board review as a treatment-planning process in which cancer physicians and other healthcare specialists meet to review and discuss new or complex cancer cases and decide as a group on the best treatment plan. Participants may include medical and radiation oncologists, surgeons, pathologists, radiologists, genetics professionals, nurses, social workers, and other specialists. The tumor board supports coordinated multidisciplinary planning; it does not eliminate the treating team's responsibilities or the client's role in informed decision-making.
candidate.source_claim_supported: NCI describes tumor board review as multidisciplinary treatment planning in which cancer physicians and other healthcare specialists review and discuss new or complex cases together; multidisciplinary cancer care includes expertise from multiple specialties and team-based care requires shared information and responsibilities.
